task: Build a new local-first freelance finance tracker phone app with Expo (React Native) for iOS and Android. Privacy is the product: all of the user's data stays on their device. There is no server, no accounts, no sign-up or login, no analytics, tracking or crash reporting, and the app never sends user data anywhere. Must-haves: (1) Policy agreement gate: on first launch, and whenever the policy version changes, the user must read the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy and tick "I agree" before anything else in the app is reachable; acceptance (policy version and date) is stored on the device. The policy says plainly that data stays on the device and the developer never receives it, that the user is responsible for their own backups, and that the app is not tax, legal or financial advice. (2) Receipts: photograph with the camera (photo-library fallback) and record amount, date, category, type (expense by default, or income) and notes; photos are kept in the app's private storage. (3) Mileage log: date, miles and purpose, with the deduction at a configurable rate per mile (default: the current IRS standard business rate, labeled "verify for your tax year"). (4) Dashboard: income, expenses, mileage deduction and estimated tax at a configurable rate (never negative), recent activity, and every primary action one tap away. (5) Exports: tax-ready CSV and PDF generated on the device and shared through the share sheet. (6) Encrypted on-device storage: the database is encrypted at rest with a key kept in the device keychain/keystore (expo-secure-store). (7) Backup and restore: export one encrypted backup file containing all records and photos, protected by a passphrase the user chooses (strong key derivation and authenticated encryption from an audited JavaScript library such as @noble/ciphers and @noble/hashes), shared wherever the user chooses (Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive); restore from such a file with the passphrase after a clear confirmation, with an integrity check and a friendly message for a wrong passphrase or damaged file. Cloud-provider sync is out of scope for now. (8) Optional app lock with Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint (expo-local-authentication), OFF by default and switchable in Settings. (9) Settings: app lock, mileage rate, tax rate, backup and restore, view the policy, and delete all data (with confirmation). The app must be visually appealing, polished and very easy to use: React Native Paper (Material 3) with a theme and shared components, generous spacing, a clear visual hierarchy, friendly empty states and a bottom tab bar to every main area. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests of the on-device logic.

issues: src/screens/ReceiptFormScreen.tsx uses raw HTML <label> and <select> elements, which violates the "react native components only" rule. Replace them with React Native components (e.g., use the Picker component for the category dropdown on all platforms, and use a Text component for the label) to ensure only React Native components are used.

The UI flow test for the policy acceptance checkbox fails because the checkbox state is not reflected as an ARIA attribute. Although the component uses `accessibilityRole="checkbox"` and `accessibilityState={{ checked }}`, the rendered element lacks the required `aria-checked` attribute, causing the test to think the checkbox never changes. Adjust the implementation to correctly toggle the `aria-checked` attribute (e.g., ensure `accessibilityState` is passed as an object with a `checked` property and verify the component updates it on press).

Static analysis reports delayed navigation caused by a `setTimeout` in the compiled bundle. This originates from navigation being performed after an async delay (e.g., navigation after policy acceptance or after saving a receipt). Modify the code to navigate immediately after the async operation completes, without wrapping it in any timeout. For example, in `src/screens/ReceiptFormScreen.tsx` replace any delayed navigation (if present) with a direct `navigation.navigate('Dashboard')` call, and ensure the policy hook navigates synchronously after checking acceptance.
review.feedback: The acceptance tests currently pass, but several static validation checks fail, preventing approval. Address the raw HTML usage, ensure the policy checkbox correctly updates its ARIA state for accessibility, and remove any delayed navigation patterns so navigation occurs immediately. Once these issues are fixed and all static checks pass, the app will meet the requirements.

ui.summary: The app fails the most critical part of the user journey – accepting the policy. The custom checkbox on PolicyScreen is missing required ARIA attributes (aria‑checked) and does not toggle its state, which leaves the Continue button permanently disabled and breaks the primary flow. Axe reports a critical violation for the same element. Several other accessibility and design‑token compliance issues were spotted (missing accessibility labels on navigation tabs, inconsistent use of theme spacing, missing autocomplete on form fields, etc.). These issues are mostly medium‑to‑low severity, but the policy‑checkbox bug must be fixed before any other quality improvements can be considered.

findings.issue: The custom checkbox is rendered as a <div> with role="checkbox" and aria-label but without the required aria-checked attribute, and its internal state never updates on click. This prevents the user from checking the box and enables the Continue button, breaking the primary onboarding flow.
findings.fix: Replace the custom element with React Native Paper's <Checkbox> (or a native <input type="checkbox">) and bind its checked state to a React state variable. Add aria-checked={checked} (or let the component handle it) and ensure the onPress toggles the state. Update the Continue button’s disabled prop based on the checked state.

findings.issue: Bottom navigation tabs are missing accessibilityLabel and explicit role="navigation". On web, focus‑visible styling is not applied, and the touch target may be smaller than the required 44 × 44 px.
findings.fix: Add accessibilityLabel to each tab (e.g., "Dashboard tab"), set role="navigation" on the container, and ensure the hit area meets the 44 px minimum (use invisible padding if needed). Add CSS for :focus-visible to show a high‑contrast outline.

findings.issue: TextInput components lack appropriate autoComplete attributes and use generic keyboardType values, which reduces form ergonomics and keyboard accessibility.
findings.fix: Pass autoComplete props that match the field purpose (e.g., autoComplete="email" for email, "off" for amount if needed) and set the correct keyboardType (numeric for amount, date for date fields).

findings.issue: When loading, the button label is replaced solely by a spinner, losing the accessible text label. The button also does not expose accessibilityState.busy.
findings.fix: Keep the button label visible when loading (e.g., "Saving receipt…") and add accessibilityState={{ busy: true }} so screen readers announce the busy state.

findings.issue: The screen wrapper does not include an explicit landmark (accessibilityRole="main") and the headline is not marked as a header, violating heading hierarchy expectations.
findings.fix: Wrap the screen content in the shared <Screen> component which should set accessibilityRole="main" and render the first headline with accessibilityRole="header". Verify the hierarchy (h1 then h2/h3).

findings.issue: Several components (e.g., SummaryCard, EmptyState) use hard‑coded spacing values like marginBottom: 16px and borderRadius: 8px instead of the defined theme.spacing and theme.roundness tokens.
findings.fix: Replace literal numbers with theme.spacing.sm / theme.roundness wherever possible to ensure consistency and easier design updates.

findings.issue: Class names are applied (e.g., "emptyState") without corresponding CSS rules, leading to unstyled elements if the CSS is missing.
findings.fix: Either define the required CSS classes in a stylesheet or remove the classNames and rely solely on the style prop (or styled-components) to apply layout.

findings.issue: The Delete confirmation dialog uses a plain TextInput for the DELETE keyword without a visible label, making it hard for screen readers to convey purpose.
findings.fix: Add a label prop to the TextInput (e.g., label="Type DELETE to confirm") and link error/helper text via accessibilityHint.

findings.issue: The entire screen is rendered with unstyled browser-defaults: plain text, no type scale, no spacing, no alignment, no visual hierarchy, no brand or design language. It looks like a raw HTML page.
findings.fix: Apply a consistent type scale with readable sizes, add generous spacing, align content to a grid, and establish visual hierarchy with typography and spacing. Use a branded color palette and design system components.

findings.issue: The content is tightly packed against the left edge, with no padding or margins, creating a cramped and unprofessional appearance. The 'Continue' button is centered but visually disconnected from the checkbox and text.
findings.fix: Add padding around the content, center the content block, and align the checkbox and button with consistent spacing. Use a grid to ensure alignment and balance.

findings.issue: The content is stretched and unbalanced, appearing as a narrow column in the center of a wide desktop viewport. There is no responsive design or layout optimization for desktop.
findings.fix: Design a desktop layout that uses the full width, with proper margins and spacing. Avoid stretching content vertically or horizontally. Use a grid or flexbox to create a balanced, professional layout.

findings.issue: The typography lacks a type scale: the title is large but the body text is tiny and not legible. The line length is too short and the text is not aligned to a grid.
findings.fix: Establish a type scale with clear hierarchy: title, body, and helper text. Use readable font sizes (e.g., 18pt for title, 14pt for body). Ensure line length is 50-75 characters and text is left-aligned on a consistent grid.

findings.issue: The checkbox and 'Continue' button are not styled or aligned properly. The button is centered but lacks visual weight or feedback to indicate it's the primary action.
findings.fix: Style the checkbox with a consistent visual weight and color. Style the 'Continue' button with a clear primary action design (e.g., bold, color, padding). Align the checkbox and button with consistent spacing and visual hierarchy.

findings.issue: visual quality 3/10 on 'policy' (needs 8+): The screen is unstyled, minimal, and appears to be browser-defaults with no design polish. It lacks visual hierarchy, spacing, and alignment that would make it feel like a polished product. The layout is cramped and unprofessional, especially on desktop where it's stretched and unbalanced. This is not acceptable for a product people would pay for.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

went_well: All unit and integration tests passed on every round, confirming that the test infrastructure is reliable.
The static validators (theme usage, TypeScript compilation, accessibility, UI primary flow) consistently caught regressions, demonstrating comprehensive coverage.
The reviewer agent produced detailed feedback each round, keeping the iteration loop active.
The pipeline respected round limits and guard thresholds, stopping after a reasonable number of attempts rather than entering an endless loop.
Design specifications (DESIGN.md, ui_flow.json) were generated early and used as a concrete reference throughout the run.

improvements.title: Make reviewer feedback precise and non-contradictory
improvements.evidence: Rounds 1-4 show contradictory guidance: round 1 recommends renaming src/navigation/index.ts to .tsx, round 2 asks for a default export, round 4 blames a circular import created by 'export { default } from "./index"', and round 5 still points to accessibility props. This back‑and‑forth caused the coder to hit turn limits (round 1, 2, 11) and wasted iterations.
improvements.change: Update the reviewer prompt to require the reviewer to (a) cite the exact line and file causing the failure, (b) propose a single minimal code change that fixes the issue, and (c) keep a short memory of previously suggested changes to avoid repetition. Add a directive: 'If you have already suggested a fix for this file, do not suggest another unless the problem persists after the fix.'
improvements.expected_effect: Reduces contradictory or redundant suggestions, allowing the coder to apply fixes efficiently and avoid hitting turn limits, thereby shortening round duration and improving convergence.

improvements.title: Add a naming‑convention validator for JSX files
improvements.evidence: The validator 'expo export' and TypeScript errors persisted from round 1 through round 10 due to JSX being placed in a .ts file (src/navigation/index.ts). The same syntax errors appear in rounds 1‑5, 8, 10, indicating the issue was not caught early.
improvements.change: Introduce a static validator (e.g., validate_file_naming.py) that scans all source files for JSX syntax (detect '<' after an import) and asserts the file extension is .tsx. Fail the round with a clear message like 'File src/navigation/index.ts contains JSX; rename to .tsx.'
improvements.expected_effect: Catches the mismatch before the coder spends many turns on compilation errors, preventing repeated TypeScript failures and reducing the number of validator blocks.

improvements.title: Enhance UI primary flow validator to report missing ARIA toggle state
improvements.evidence: Validator 'ui primary flow' blocked 11 of 12 rounds. The failure consistently mentions the policy checkbox never changing state (round 2, 12). Reviewer kept suggesting changes to the Pressable component but the core problem – missing aria‑checked/accessible toggle – remained.
improvements.change: Extend ui_flow validation to (a) explicitly check that the element identified by its label has an accessible checked state that toggles on click, (b) when the check fails, output a suggestion such as 'Ensure the checkbox component sets aria‑checked (or accessibilityState.checked) and uses a component that supports it, e.g., React Native Paper Checkbox.'
improvements.expected_effect: Provides the coder with a direct, actionable fix for the primary flow, reducing the number of iterations needed to get the flow passing.

improvements.title: Allow dynamic coder turn limit increase for persistent compile‑time failures
improvements.evidence: Coder hit its turn limit in rounds 1, 2, 11 (each lasting >30 min). In round 1 and 2 the issue was a naming error; in round 11 it was delayed navigation refactoring. The fixed turn cap forced the coder to stop mid‑fix, extending the overall run time.
improvements.change: Modify the coder turn‑limit policy to detect when a round ends due to 'turn limit reached' and the failing validator is a compile‑time error (e.g., TypeScript). In such cases automatically grant an additional 20‑30 turns for that round before applying the nudges limit.
improvements.expected_effect: Gives the coder enough room to perform larger refactorings (renaming files, moving imports) without being cut off, reducing the need for extra rounds and speeding overall convergence.

improvements.title: Synchronize DESIGN.md labels with component accessibility names
improvements.evidence: Throughout rounds the UI flow test looked for the label 'I agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.' The checkbox component did not expose a matching accessible name, leading to timeout failures in every round (ui primary flow). The designer spec and implementation were out of sync.
improvements.change: Revise the designer prompt to generate a mapping file (e.g., accessibility_map.json) that lists each interactive element’s accessible label as defined in DESIGN.md. Add a validator that cross‑checks component code for these labels, failing early if mismatched.
improvements.expected_effect: Ensures that design specifications and code stay aligned, preventing UI flow failures caused by label mismatches and reducing the number of revisions needed.
